title: REC-22: Save only complete recipes
description: Save stays disabled until the recipe has a title, at least one ingredient, at least one step, and a duration on every step. The toolbar says what's missing: “Step I has no duration”.
acceptance_criteria:
- Rust computes the missing-items list and the first message. Table-driven Rust tests over the D-37 rules.
- Old incomplete recipes still open; they must be completed before their next save (E-02).
- Snapshot: disabled Save with message.

title: REC-20: Steps use ingredient lines
description: The inspector's **Uses** adds “2 tbsp olive oil” to “Fry onion & garlic”. The read view shows each step's ingredients under it.
acceptance_criteria: - Migration adds step-uses-line links. Removing a line or step removes its uses (Q-R2). Snapshots: inspector Uses, read view.

title: REC-21: One-cook total time
description: The list row reads “Roasted tomato pasta · 38 min · 8 steps”, and so does the read view. 38 min is one pair of hands: active steps never overlap, while waiting steps run in the background. That compares to 35 min for the longest chain and 59 min for the plain sum.
acceptance_criteria:
- Pure Rust one-cook scheduler, tested on the mockup's example (38 min) and edge cases. Prep counts (D-33).
- While any step has no duration (possible before REC-22), the total shows “—”.
- Snapshot: list rows with totals.

title: REC-19: The read view shows stages
description: The read view groups steps by what can start together: “1 · Dice onion, Mince garlic, Boil water”, then “2 · Fry onion & garlic”…
acceptance_criteria: - Pure Rust stage function with tests (diamonds, loose ends, single step). Order within a stage per Q-R3. Snapshot: staged read view.

title: REC-17: Duration, active/waiting and instructions
description: The inspector sets “6 min”, **Active** or **Waiting**, and optional instructions (“Medium heat, stir often”). Active nodes are solid, waiting nodes dashed. The read view shows each step's duration.
acceptance_criteria:
- A duration is one positive value (D-21); a new step has none until set (Q-R5).
- Rust tests for parsing and validation. Snapshots: active and waiting nodes, inspector filled in.

title: REC-18: Connect steps into a graph
description: Drag from the ● on “Dice onion” to the ○ on “Fry onion & garlic”: an arrow appears, and the inspector's **After** lists “Dice onion”. A connection that would make a loop snaps back. Click an arrow and press [[⌫]] to remove it.
acceptance_criteria:
- Migration adds step edges. Rust rejects cycles, self-loops and duplicates, with property-style tests for the cycle check.
- Several loose ends are fine (D-22). Snapshots: connected graph, port-drag preview.

title: REC-16: Delete a step
description: Select a node and press [[⌫]], or right-click it ▸ **Delete step**. It disappears, along with its connections once those exist.
acceptance_criteria: - Rust removes the step and anything that refers to it. Rust tests; snapshot of the context menu.

title: REC-14: Add steps on a canvas
description: The editor shows a canvas. Right-click on empty space ▸ **Add step** places a node where you clicked. Selecting a node opens the inspector, where you type its title (“Dice onion”). The read view lists the steps, and the list row shows “3 steps”.
design:
Stubs until later slices:
- Nodes can't be moved yet (REC-15) or deleted (REC-16).
- The inspector shows Duration, Instructions and After as disabled placeholders (REC-17, REC-18).
- The read view shows a flat list; stages come in REC-19.
acceptance_criteria:
- Migration adds steps (UUID, recipe, title, x, y). Positions are Rust state, saved with the recipe.
- A step needs a title. Rust tests: add, select, rename, step count.
- Snapshots: canvas with nodes, inspector. UI smoke: add a step via the context menu and save.

title: REC-15: Move steps on the canvas
description: You drag “Dice onion” to a new place; after saving and reopening, it's still there.
acceptance_criteria: - Swift owns only the drag in progress and sends one move event on drop. Rust test for moves; UI smoke: drag, save, reopen.

title: REC-13: Deleting a catalog ingredient that recipes use
description: Deleting “tomato” from the catalog says “It's linked from 3 recipes. Their lines keep their text and lose the link.” After deleting, those lines read “400 g Mutti tomatoes”, unlinked.
acceptance_criteria:
- Deleting an ingredient clears links in the same transaction. The count comes from the store.
- Catalog detail widget shows the count. Snapshot: catalog delete confirmation with count.

title: REC-11: Catalog suggestions while typing
description: Typing “Mutti tom” offers “tomato” and “canned tomatoes”; one click links it. A saved unlinked line with a likely match shows a suggestion chip “→ tomato?” (Q-R6).
acceptance_criteria: - Matching runs in Rust against catalog name keys. Rust tests for ranking and the likely-match rule. Snapshots: suggestion list, chip.

title: REC-12: The linked ingredient's units in the picker
description: When a line links to “garlic”, the unit picker also offers “clove ≈ 5 g”, taken from the catalog.
acceptance_criteria:
- Choosing a reference unit stores it by name; if the link is removed later, the line keeps the unit as custom text.
- Snapshot: picker with reference units.

title: REC-10: Link a line to a catalog ingredient
description: In the line editor you pick a catalog ingredient, so the line reads “400 g Mutti tomatoes → tomato”. **Unlink** removes the link. Unlinked lines show a quiet “no link”.
design:
Stubs until later slices:
- The picker is a plain searchable list for now; suggestions while typing come in REC-11.
acceptance_criteria:
- Nullable link from line to ingredient. The line keeps its own name (D-11).
- Snapshots: linked and unlinked lines.

title: REC-08: Amount, known unit and note on a line
description: A line becomes “300 g penne pasta” or “1 tbsp olive oil, extra virgin”. The unit picker offers g, kg, ml, l, tsp, tbsp, cup and piece. Amount and unit are optional, so “salt, to taste” works.
acceptance_criteria:
- Exact decimal amounts (catalog rules). Unit present without amount, or a non-positive amount, is a typed issue.
